title: Crypto & IDs
summary: UUID v4/v7 and ULIDs, SHA hashes, HMAC webhook signatures with a stored secret, base64/hex/URL encoding, random and one-time codes, and HS256 JWTs.
description:
Crypto & IDs gives workflows identifiers and cryptography from the server's secure random generator. Generate random UUID v4s or time-ordered UUID v7s and ULIDs that sort by creation time, unbiased random codes from alphabets without look-alike characters (grouped like ABCD-EFGH), and numeric one-time codes with an expiry time and a hash to store instead of the code. Hash text with SHA-256, SHA-512, SHA-384 or SHA-1 and encode or decode base64, base64url, hex and URL percent-encoding.

For integrations, HMAC signs a message with a key that an administrator stores once (hmac_key): the host computes the signature, so the key never reaches workflow builders or the action's code, and a received webhook signature is compared in constant time. Sign token and Verify token issue and check compact HS256 JSON Web Tokens with token_secret: expiry, not-before, issuer and audience are enforced, and invalid tokens come back with a reason instead of failing the workflow.
uses: Verify the HMAC signature of an incoming webhook before processing it
Issue a signed, expiring link token for an external approver and check it when they respond
Generate voucher or reference codes and time-ordered IDs for new records
setup: Install the package: the action appears in Extensibility → Workflow actions and in the workflow designer's palette under Custom actions.
For HMAC: in Extensibility → Workflow actions, open Crypto & IDs and set the hmac_key secret (e.g. your webhook provider's signing secret). For tokens: set token_secret to a long random value.
Drag Crypto & IDs onto a workflow and choose the function. For webhooks, map Message to the raw request body and Signature to check to the signature header, then branch on {{prefix_matches}}.
Try the included "Signed approval link (sample)" workflow from the API or its start form after setting token_secret: it signs a token for an approver, verifies it and hashes the request reference.
